description: Explores the deep mathematical parallels between statistical physics, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, spin-glass models, and the computational dynamics of artificial neural networks.
learning_objectives: Understand statistical mechanics formulations of neural associative memories and spin glass models.
Analyze energy landscapes, attractor dynamics in Hopfield networks, and Boltzmann machines.
Connect non-equilibrium thermodynamics, Langevin dynamics, and score-based diffusion models.
Apply information geometry, renormalization group methods, and Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs).
outline: Statistical Mechanics of Neural Networks: Spin glass models, Ising model, energy landscapes, mean field theory, replicas.
Energy-Based Models: Hopfield networks, associative memory capacity, attractor dynamics, Boltzmann machines, Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs).
Thermodynamics & Non-Equilibrium Systems: Free energy minimization, Langevin dynamics, Fokker-Planck equations, score-based diffusion models.
Dynamical Systems & Chaos: Neural dynamics, stability analysis, chaos in recurrent neural networks, reservoir computing.
Information Geometry & Physics of Learning: Information bottleneck theory, renormalization group in deep networks, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs).
